paper_title: Searching for an oscillating massive scalar field as a dark matter candidate using atomic hyperfine frequency comparisons
coupling_convention: dimensionless d_e (paper's limit is on the combination de + 0.043(d_mhat - d_g), which equals d_e under the assumption of coupling to electromagnetism only)
notes: Hees et al. (2016, arXiv:1604.08514): 6 years of Rb/Cs hyperfine frequency ratio data from the FO2 dual atomic fountain at LNE-SYRTE, searching for oscillating scalar dark matter. Explicit anchor points from text: most stringent limit 3.8e-9 at m_phi = 1.4e-23 eV; worst-case limit 5.3e-4 anywhere in range; mass range ~1e-24 to ~2.4e-18 eV (omega_max = 3.6e-3 rad/s). Intermediate points reconstructed from the stated frequency-dependent noise levels (Eq. 9) and Eq. 8 scaling (coupling limit ∝ omega x amplitude limit), so they are approximate — the true exclusion curve in Fig. 3 is jagged. The constrained quantity is the combination de + 0.043(d_mhat - d_g); classified as ScalarPhoton per the paper's headline interpretation (assuming only de != 0, improving Dy limits by >1 order of magnitude).
